info.name: Clio API Documentation Activities Bills API
Returns the pre-rendered html for the Bill

params.name: id
params.description: The unique identifier for the Bill.

items.docs:
This endpoint returns a pre-rendered HTML object that you can use to view a preview of your bills.
The HTML provided contains all of the CSS rules it requires to show the bill correctly,
as well as the DOCTYPE setting it requires.
It's best to use an iframe, or similar object, to render the results of this endpoint.

info.name: Return the data for all Bills

params.name: bill_number
params.description: Filter Bill records to those with this exact bill number

params.name: client_id
params.description: The unique identifier for a single Contact. The keyword `null` is not valid for this field. The list will be filtered to include only the Bill records with the matching property.

params.name: created_since
params.description: Filter Bill records to those having the `created_at` field after a specific time. (Expects an ISO-8601 timestamp).

params.name: currency_id
params.description: Filter Bill records to those of a specific currency.

params.name: custom_field_values
params.description:
Filter records to only those with the given custom field(s) set. The value is compared using the operator provided, or,
if the value type only supports one operator, the supported operator is used. In the latter case, no check for operator is performed on the input string.
The key for the custom field value filter is the custom_field.id. e.g. `custom_field_values[12345]`
If an operator is used for a type that does not support it, an `400 Bad Request` is returned.

*Supported operators:*
* `checkbox`, `contact`, `matter`, `picklist` : `=`

e.g. `?custom_field_values[1]=42`

* `currency`, `date`, `time`, `numeric` : `=`, `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=`

e.g. `?custom_field_values[1]=>=105.4`

* `email`, `text_area`, `text_line`, `url` : `=`

e.g. `?custom_field_values[1]=url_encoded`

*Multiple conditions for the same custom field:*

If you want to use more than one operator to filter a custom field, you can do so by passing in an array of values.
e.g. `?custom_field_values[1]=[<=50, >=45]`

params.name: due_after
params.description: Filter Bill records to those that have a `due_date` after the one provided (Expects an ISO-8601 date).

params.name: due_at
params.description: Filter Bill records to those that have a specific `due_date` (Expects an ISO-8601 date).

params.name: due_before
params.description: Filter Bill records to those that have a `due_date` before the one provided (Expects an ISO-8601 date).

params.name: fields
params.description: The fields to be returned. See response samples for what fields are available. For more information see the [fields section](#section/Fields).

params.name: ids[]
params.description: Filter Bill records to those having the specified unique identifiers.

params.name: issued_after
params.description: Filter Bill records to those that have an `issue_date` after the one provided (Expects an ISO-8601 date).

params.name: issued_before
params.description: Filter Bill records to those that have an `issue_date` before the one provided (Expects an ISO-8601 date).

params.name: last_sent_end_date
params.description: Filter Bill records for those whose bills have been sent before the specified date

params.name: last_sent_start_date
params.description: Filter Bill records for those whose bills have been sent after the specified date

params.name: limit
params.description: A limit on the number of Bill records to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 200. Default: `200`.

params.name: matter_id
params.description: The unique identifier for a single Matter. Use the keyword `null` to match those without a Bill. The list will be filtered to include only the Bill records with the matching property.

params.name: order
params.description: Orders the Bill records by the given field. Default: `id(asc)`.

params.name: originating_attorney_id
params.description: The unique identifier for a single User. Use the keyword `null` to match those without a Bill. The list will be filtered to include only the Bill records with the matching property.

params.name: overdue_only
params.description: Filter Bill records to those that are overdue.

params.name: page_token
params.description: A token specifying which page to return.

params.name: query
params.description: Allows matching search on invoice number.

params.name: responsible_attorney_id
params.description: The unique identifier for a single User. Use the keyword `null` to match those without a Bill. The list will be filtered to include only the Bill records with the matching property.

params.name: state
params.description: Filter Bill records to those in a given state.

params.name: status
params.description: Filter Bill records to those with particular payment status.

params.name: type
params.description: Filter Bill records to those of a specific type.

params.name: updated_since
params.description: Filter Bill records to those having the `updated_at` field after a specific time. (Expects an ISO-8601 timestamp).

items.docs:
This endpoint will transition a bill to either its deleted or voided state.
A bill can only be deleted or voided if it has no payments recorded
and its current state is one of the following:
* Draft
* Pending Approval
* Unpaid

A bill will automatically be moved to a deleted or void state based on its current state.
The mappings for this are:
* Draft -> Deleted
* Pending Approval -> Deleted
* Unpaid -> Void
